The real deliverable: take a credit-scoring model that *drops* the protected
attribute, show it still leaks, then neutralize it and report the group gap
before and after.  Data is the Adult-census-shaped set (`sex` protected,
`income_high` target, plus proxy features).

---

## 1 · The Gap, and the Proxy Channels

```{python}
adult = datasets.load_adult_like()
print(f"loaded {len(adult)} rows")
m, f = adult[adult.sex == 1], adult[adult.sex == 0]
print(f"P(high income | sex=1) = {m.income_high.mean():.2f}")
print(f"P(high income | sex=0) = {f.income_high.mean():.2f}   ← the gap to neutralize")
print()
for c in ["age", "education_num", "hours_per_week", "occupation_prestige"]:
    print(f"corr({c:<20}, sex) = {adult[c].corr(adult.sex):+.2f}   (a proxy channel)")
```

## 2 · Baseline: Drop `sex`, and Watch It Leak

Train a scorecard on the proxy features only — `sex` is never an input — then
audit the score against `sex` with CKA.

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
CKA builds an $n \times n$ kernel matrix, so we work on a representative 2 000-row
sample (the group gap above is computed on the full data).  The fair-kernel
library does this with mini-batches during training.
:::

```{python}
sample = adult.sample(n=2000, random_state=0).reset_index(drop=True)
feat = ["age", "education_num", "hours_per_week", "occupation_prestige"]
X = sample[feat].to_numpy(dtype=float)
X = (X - X.mean(0)) / X.std(0)
y = sample["income_high"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
S = sample["sex"].to_numpy(dtype=float)

# Composite baseline score from the legitimate features (sex excluded).
w, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(np.column_stack([X, np.ones(len(X))]), y, rcond=None)
score = np.column_stack([X, np.ones(len(X))]) @ w

print(f"baseline (sex dropped):  CKA(score, sex) = {cka_rbf(score, S):.2f}   ← still leaks")
```

The leak is visible: the two groups get systematically different scores even
though `sex` was never an input.

```{python}
#| label: fig-jobB-leak
#| fig-cap: "Baseline score distribution by group. Despite dropping `sex`, the groups get systematically different scores — the proxies carried it through."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 4.0))
for g, col, name in [(0, COOL, "sex = 0"), (1, WARM, "sex = 1")]:
    ax.hist(score[S == g], bins=30, density=True, alpha=0.55, color=col, label=name)
    ax.axvline(score[S == g].mean(), color=col, lw=2, ls="--")
ax.set_xlabel("baseline score"); ax.set_ylabel("density")
ax.set_title(f"Score leaks the dropped attribute · CKA = {cka_rbf(score, S):.2f}",
             fontsize=12)
ax.legend(fontsize=9, frameon=False); despine(ax)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## 3 · Neutralize, and Sweep the Trade-Off

`fair_fit` re-fits `income_high` from the baseline score while penalizing
dependence on `sex`.

```{python}
def group_gap(pred):
    return pred[S == 1].mean() - pred[S == 0].mean()

def utility(pred):
    return float(np.corrcoef(pred, y)[0, 1])  # rank-ish utility vs the target

sweep = [0.0, 0.5, 2.0, 8.0, 20.0]
print(f"{'μ':>6}{'CKA(score,sex)':>16}{'group gap':>12}{'utility':>10}")
print("-" * 44)
cka_s, gaps, utils = [], [], []
for mu in sweep:
    p = fair_fit(score, y, S, mu=mu)
    cs, g, u = cka_rbf(p, S), group_gap(p), utility(p)
    cka_s.append(cs); gaps.append(g); utils.append(u)
    print(f"{mu:>6g}{cs:>16.3f}{g:>+12.3f}{u:>10.3f}")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-jobB-neutralize
#| fig-cap: "Left: the group gap in mean score shrinks as μ grows. Right: utility vs neutrality — the frontier on real credit data."
fig, (axL, axR) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11.5, 4.3))

axL.plot(sweep, np.abs(gaps), "-o", c=CRASH, lw=2.2)
axL.set_xlabel("neutrality weight μ"); axL.set_ylabel("|group gap| in mean score")
axL.set_title("The group gap closes", fontsize=12)
despine(axL)

axR.plot(cka_s, utils, "-o", c=COOL, lw=2.2)
for mu, cx, uy in zip(sweep, cka_s, utils):
    axR.annotate(f"μ={mu:g}", (cx, uy), textcoords="offset points",
                 xytext=(6, 5), fontsize=9, color=INK)
axR.set_xlabel("CKA(score, sex)  →  less neutral")
axR.set_ylabel("utility (corr with income)")
axR.set_title("Utility vs neutrality", fontsize=12)
despine(axR)

fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## The Deliverable
Report the *operating point*, not a single model: "at μ = … we cut CKA from
its baseline to … and the group gap from … to …, keeping … of baseline utility."
The choice of μ is a policy decision — the maths only gives you the frontier.
:::
